newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: WTO's Ruggiero praises Mercosur, looks to expansion.
newsitem.headline: WTO's Ruggiero praises Mercosur, looks to expansion.

text.p: Renato Ruggiero, the Director- General of the World Trade Organization, on Wednesday praised the progress of the Mercosur customs union in its drive to expand trade liberalization in Latin America.

"Once you create a successful process like Mercosur you will inevitably see that this will be the core of the process of a Latin American regional process," Ruggiero told Reuters in an interview at the half-yearly meeting of Mercosur presidents held in Asuncion.

Mercosur was established by Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay in 1991. Bolivia and Chile have free trade agreements with the group and talks are in the offing for deals with the Andean countries of Ecuador, Peru and Venezuala in addition to Mexico.

The head of the world trade body welcomed prospects of the expansion of Mercosur adding that at "a certain moment I see it connecting itself with the NAFTA (the free trade area grouping the United State, Canada and Mexico) program into an American Free Trade Area (AFTA)."

The heads of state of 34 countries across the Americas agreed in December 1994 to work towards the implementation of AFTA in 2005. Mercosur leaders are expected to firm up their common position on AFTA at this week's meeting.

Furthermore, Ruggiero said "it is very important that for the first time the Mercosur has invited the Director-General of the WTO. It shows that this process wants to remain not only compatible with but as a way to strengthening the multilateral trading system."
He said the openness of the Mercosur to world trade rather than sheltered regionalism is what he will underline when he addresses the Mercosur presidents Thursday.
"Of course that is what interests me more than anything -- that there is an open regionalism, a regionalism that is ready to have contacts with all the rest of the world."

Asked about the introduction by Brazil in March of restrictions on import financing of less than a year which led to a diplomatic spat betwee Brazil and its Mercosur partners, Ruggiero said he hoped a solution can be found.
"I hope this Mercosur meeting will be the occasion to try to settle or at least make progress in the direction of settling this question," he said.
Brazil agreed to ease the restrictions for Mercosur imports until July and diplomats at the Asuncion meeting hinted that a solution would be found.

"Very frankly the question has not been brought yet to the dispute settlement procedure (of the WTO) - there has been a statement from the United States expressing some concern but no more than that," Ruggiero added.

Rugggiero agreed that so-called U.S. presidential fast-track negotiating powers would be an important addition to U.S. trade policy. Talks on the inclusion of Chile into NAFTA have been held up because President Clinton has not yet got approval from Congress on fast-track powers.
"It (fast-track) would be a very important signal of the intention to lead the process of liberalization in the next few years," Ruggiero said.

The WTO head pointed out that integration of Mercosur is going at a rapid pace, even faster than that of Asia's ASEAN trade bloc. "There is even talk of a single currency -- there are a lot ambitions," he said.
He added that Mercosur's has been "very succesful," not least because of the impact it has on countries like Paraguay, the poorest of the Mercosur partners.

"Take the case of a small country like Paraguay, which in a certain sense is coming out of a completely different political system and is now moving into democracy and towards opening up its economy. This process is made easier by Paraguay belonging to Mercosur," he said.

Most of all, the "Mercosur is very successful and from this point of view the dynamic that it could inject in the liberalisation process of this part of the world is extremely interesting for us in the multilateral system," Ruggiero said.
